name: Oni
origin: Japanese folklore and Buddhist hell imagery, Japan
looks: Huge horned brute with red, blue or black skin, tusks, claws and an iron-studded club.
behavior: Lives in caves and mountains, eats people and brings plague and war; also a hell warden in Buddhist art.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Oni faces are also used as protective charms and in setsubun rites, so do not mock those rites; the monster itself is widely used in fiction.
reads_at_16x20: yes: horns and club give a clear silhouette

name: Tengu
looks: Red-faced or crow-headed winged figure in mountain ascetic dress with a feather fan; early forms were kite-like.
behavior: Medieval Buddhist tales cast them as proud demons that mislead monks with false visions, possess people and abduct priests.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Some tengu are revered as mountain guardians in Shugendo and at shrines; use the malevolent medieval form and avoid sacred priest imagery. Unverified, one source.

name: Kappa
looks: Child-sized green scaly water imp with a turtle shell, beak and a water-filled dish on its head.
behavior: Older tales have it drowning people and livestock and pulling out the mythical shirikodama; spilling its dish weakens it.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Widely used in fiction; some shrines honor kappa as water spirits, so keep it a pest, not a deity. Unverified, one source.

name: Umibozu
looks: Giant black bald humanoid that rises head and shoulders from a calm sea at night, eyes glittering.
behavior: Lifts out of still water, whips up a storm and swamps ships, often by scooping water in with a ladle.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Folklore monster widely used in fiction.
reads_at_16x20: yes: huge round dark head over waves

name: Funayurei
looks: Glowing ghosts of the drowned, or ghost lights and phantom ships, over a stormy sea.
behavior: Appear on foggy or stormy nights, ask ships for a ladle to flood them, and lure boats to danger with false lights.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Ghost folklore, widely used.
reads_at_16x20: yes: pale figure with ladle; overlaps Wraith in role

name: Yamauba
looks: Wild crone in a tattered kimono with long matted hair and, in some tales, a mouth on top of her head.
behavior: Waylays travelers on mountain paths to eat them; some tales also show her granting fortune.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Folklore monster; some regions worship her as a house god, so use the hostile form.
reads_at_16x20: yes: hunched hag with wild hair

name: Rokurokubi
looks: Ordinary-looking woman whose neck stretches, or whose head detaches and flies at night.
behavior: Flying heads hunt insects and sometimes people at night and must rejoin the body before dawn (Hearn's Rokuro-Kubi tale).
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Widely used folklore.
reads_at_16x20: yes: floating head with trailing neck

name: Yuki-onna
looks: Tall pale woman in white with long black hair and blue lips who leaves no footprints in snow.
behavior: Freezes travelers with her breath or leads them astray in blizzards; Hearn's tale has her sparing a boy.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Widely used in fiction.
reads_at_16x20: yes: white robed figure with a cold breath cloud

name: Nue
looks: Chimera with a monkey head, tiger limbs, tanuki body and snake tail, or a mix of cat, fox and chicken parts.
behavior: Shrieks like a bird at night, shifts into a black cloud, and its cry was an ill omen for emperors in the Heike legend.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Folklore chimera, widely used. Unverified, one source.
reads_at_16x20: yes: snake-tailed beast in a dark cloud

name: Tsuchigumo
looks: Giant cave spider whose belly holds many skulls, or a woman who sheds her disguise.
behavior: Hides in caves, shapeshifts into a beautiful woman to trap warriors and summons illusions.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: The name also described historical rebel clans of ancient Japan, so never tie the monster to any real people. Unverified, one source.

name: Jorogumo
looks: Spider that appears as a beautiful woman, drawn with small spiders at her command.
behavior: Lures men in disguise or drags them into waterfalls with her web, then eats them.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Widely used folklore.
reads_at_16x20: yes: spider body with a woman's torso

name: Gashadokuro
looks: Skeleton more than ten meters tall, made of skulls of people who died unburied in battle or famine.
behavior: Walks at night clacking its teeth and bites people it sees; Shinto charms are said to ward it off.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written. The page says it first appeared in print in 1966, so its age as folklore is unverified. Folklore age unverified: first known records are modern or only the film/20th-century source was read.
sensitivity_note: Widely used in fiction.

name: Nekomata
looks: Large cat-eyed beast with two tails, dog-sized or larger.
behavior: Eats people, shapeshifts, and raises and controls the dead with paw and tail dances.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Widely used in fiction.
reads_at_16x20: yes: two tails and feline ears

name: Kamaitachi
looks: Weasel-like beast with blade forelimbs that rides whirlwinds.
behavior: Slashes legs painlessly so wounds bleed later; said to live in puddles.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Widely used folklore.
reads_at_16x20: yes: small weasel with sickle arms and dust trail

name: Shuten-doji
looks: Giant red oni king with five horns and fifteen eyes in the oldest text.
behavior: Leads oni who abduct young women from Kyoto; slain by Minamoto no Raiko in a famous legend.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written. Medieval tale.
sensitivity_note: Medieval legendary figure. Unverified, one source.

name: Namazu
looks: Enormous catfish beneath Japan that thrashes to cause earthquakes; drawn serpent-like in some 1855 prints.
behavior: Pinned down by the Kashima god with a rock; thrashes if the guard slips.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Tied to Kashima shrine belief, and after 1855 it was honored in prints as a 'world rectifier'; usable with care. Unverified, one source.

name: Nogitsune
looks: Wild fox with several tails and a fox-fire glow.
behavior: Tricks travelers, shapeshifts into people, and possesses victims, causing illness.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Kitsune serve the deity Inari, a living Shinto tradition; use only the wild nogitsune form, never an Inari fox or shrine imagery.

name: Jikininki
looks: Gaunt ghost of a greedy priest, reborn as a corpse eater.
behavior: Creeps into villages at night to devour the dead (Hearn's Jikininki tale).
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Buddhist moral tale, widely used.

name: Namahage
looks: Giant red or blue oni mask, straw cloak and knife.
behavior: Walks door to door on New Year's Eve scolding lazy children; a visiting-deity ritual.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: A living New Year ritual, considered a visiting toshigami deity; not an enemy. Listed for the owner only. Unverified, one source.

name: Akkorokamui
looks: Giant red octopus-like sea monster, about 100 meters across.
behavior: Lurks in Funka Bay and swallows or capsizes ships.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Name includes kamuy (god) and the Ainu are a living culture; the page marks claims of reverence as disputed. Treat as not an enemy until the owner decides. Unverified, one source.
reads_at_16x20: yes: tentacle mass, but red by sensitivity

name: Jiangshi
looks: Stiff greenish-gray corpse in an official's robe with a paper talisman on the forehead.
behavior: Hunts the living for their vital energy, can hop or fly when old, and fears peach wood, mirrors and a rooster's crow.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Widely used in fiction. Unverified, one source.
reads_at_16x20: yes: arms out, talisman, tall hat

name: Taotie
other_names: gluttonous beast | one of the Four Perils
origin: Chinese myth, China (Shan Hai Jing; Zuo Zhuan)
looks: Greedy wolf-like beast with a huge mouth, famous from bronze vessel art.
behavior: Devours the old and feeble but fears groups; a symbol of greed.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Bronze taotie masks are ancestral ritual art; use the hungry beast, not the vessel designs.

name: Qiongqi
looks: Winged tiger-like beast, or an ox with hedgehog fur.
behavior: Eats people and, in later texts, punishes the just and feeds the wicked.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Evil beast of the Four Perils; low risk.

name: Xiangliu
looks: Venomous nine-headed serpent; modern art makes it hydra-like.
behavior: Turns every place it rests or touches into poisoned, dead bog; serves the flood god Gonggong.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Evil monster of flood myth.
reads_at_16x20: yes: nine heads on one body

name: Bashe
looks: Giant python in green, yellow, red or black.
behavior: Swallows elephants whole and spits up the bones after three years.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Monster snake; low risk. Unverified, one source.

name: Xingtian
looks: Headless warrior with eyes on his chest and a mouth at his navel, holding axe and shield.
behavior: After losing to Huangdi and being beheaded, he fights on.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Described as a deity and a symbol of defiance; not an enemy. Listed for the owner only. Unverified, one source.

name: Gonggong
looks: Red-haired, copper-headed, serpent-bodied water god.
behavior: Floods the land and smashed Buzhou Mountain, tilting the sky.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: A deity (a malevolent water god); never an enemy. Listed for the owner only.

name: Hungry ghost
origin: Chinese Buddhist and folk belief, China and diaspora
looks: Gaunt ghost with a thin neck and huge hunger.
behavior: Roams in the seventh lunar month for food and can possess and sicken the living.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Living Ghost Festival rite honoring the dead; handle with respect. Werner (PG 15250) also records the hungry ghosts released at the festival.

name: Nian
looks: Lion-like beast with a flat face and sharp teeth, bigger than an elephant in some tales.
behavior: Emerges at New Year to eat livestock and children; fears loud noise, fire and red.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written. Folklore age unverified: first known records are modern or only the film/20th-century source was read.
sensitivity_note: Tied to Lunar New Year customs; the page says the earliest written sources are from the early 20th century (age unverified). Unverified, one source.

name: Huli jing
looks: Fox with nine tails, or a beautiful woman.
behavior: Seduces scholars, drains vitality, and possesses or confuses people.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Fox spirits are venerated in some regional folk religion (unverified in these sources); use the malicious tales.

name: Dokkaebi
looks: Fearsome horned figure from roof-tile art, in hanbok, arriving with blue flame.
behavior: Challenges travelers to wrestle, plays tricks, and is blamed for fires and disease; owns an invisibility hat and a wishing club.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: The page also calls them nature spirits who bring luck; use the trickster and wrestler. Unverified, one source.

name: Gumiho
looks: Nine-tailed fox, or a beautiful woman.
behavior: Drains the life of virtuous men, feeds on blood and organs, and is a rival to dragons.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Widely used folklore.

name: Imugi
looks: Huge serpent, like a hornless dragon.
behavior: Lives in water or caves and becomes a dragon after a thousand years; modern fiction makes it evil.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written. Do not copy the film D-War designs.
sensitivity_note: Sighting is considered good luck and it is a pre-dragon in belief; the evil form comes from fiction. Unverified, one source.

name: Bulgasari
looks: Iron-eating monster; the film shows a dragon-like beast.
behavior: Eats iron and tools in the legend; the film makes it a vengeful resurrected man.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written. CAUTION: the page cites the 1962 film and 1985 remake; the legend's age is unverified. Do not use the film look. Folklore age unverified: first known records are modern or only the film/20th-century source was read.
sensitivity_note: Folk legend, modern film popularization. Unverified, one source.
reads_at_16x20: yes: iron-eater, but needs an original look

behavior: Ghost of a woman who died unmarried; floats without legs.
license_note: Myth, folklore or cryptid; own description written.
sensitivity_note: Tied to funeral and ancestor beliefs; use as a generic ghost. Unverified, one source.

sensitivity_note: Folklore ghost. Unverified, one source.
